title: Saving documents in Draft Mode
text:
Saving documents in Draft Mode 
 N avigation in Farvision 
 Saving documents in draft mode 
 Draft mode allows users to temporarily save typed data without storing the data in the actual transactional database. Large transactions can be saved in interim state as Draft mode for future use. User can resume re-entry of transactions from draft mode. 
 Transactions within draft mode are not available for any further subsequent processing. Draft Mode has to be set as ‘ON’ in the interface for Draft mode saving button to be enabled. There is no such setting required for Draft mode enabling. It is enabled by code only. 
 ‘Save As Draft’ is enabled under submit menu. 
 After a document is saved as draft, user can only retrieve it again after making draft mode on in the same interface. 
 Click on the row to open the screen and make further entry or necessary changes. After that user is required to finally submit and save the entry. 
 ©

title: Queue Management for Reports
text:
Queue Management for Reports 
 Some common features of Farvision 
 Queue Management for Reports 
 Queue management allows for processing of data in the background so that the user does not have to wait while data is being processed. Once the report or process is completed a notification will be provided that the job has been completed. It is important to use queues so that server utilization is not disturbed during peak working hours. 
 There are two types of queues 
 Queue Reports 
 Queue Processes 
 Notifications 
 Desktop notification will be shown after completion of job. Report can be downloaded from the notification alert. Queue Reports 
Some reports and bulk print format can be queued. There are two types of processes 
 ● Fire and forget - the queue is started on demand when the report has to be processed 
 ● Repeat every few minutes - any data which is added for the bulk processing will be processed, and checking for new data will be done on a predefined frequency. 
 Fire and forget 
 A job id is assigned against reports which are being queued under fire and forget. A notification will be sent to the user’s device once the report is ready. Reports which have been queued can only be printed from the Queue management console. Queued reports cannot be printed (either PDF or Excel) from the menu interface from which generation of report was started. 
 Example : Application detail register, Booking register, Invoice register and Receipt register, Indent register, Purchase order register, Goods receipt Note register and Purchase Bill register. Examples for Bulk Printing of documents are Invoice, Booking annexure, Applicant Ledger. 
 Repeat every few minutes 
Queues which repeat every few minutes are used for bulk printing of documents. No job id assigned as it is a continuous loop where more documents which are added for bulk processes are picked up. After receiving the notification, search Bulk Printing in the menu column and then for the relevant menu Item. 
 Download : Once the report is complete, it can be downloaded and saved locally. The report will be automatically deleted after downloading. Reports will be visible in the queue console until the reports are downloaded. Users are allowed to download their reports while admin users can download report of any user. 
 Delete : Pending and generated report can be deleted. If the status is pending, the delete button will stop the processing of the report. If the status is Complete, delete will physically remove the report and it will not be available, it is deleted from the server. 
 Status : Pending, In Process, Complete, Error, No record found are the status of the queued report. 
 Remarks : This column provides details of the status. Example, For In process, it will show start. 
 Desktop notification will be shown after completion of the job. Hide Downloaded : On select of the Hide Downloaded check box, all downloaded row items will be hidden and only those row items will be shown which are pending for download. Queue Process 
 Some reports a process has to be run before the report can be generated. 
 Example : Finance module cash flow report generated through process method and process report will be downloaded from queue console under the Process tab. 
 Property management invoice generated through bulk invoice menu after notification will be downloaded from the queue console. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Data Import Process
text:
Data Import Process 
 Some common features of Farvision 
 Data Import Process 
 Data import allows data to be imported from excel sheets instead of entering through the interface. Data has to be entered in pre-defined excel sheets, checked for correctness and is then imported into Farvision. Data import is available for many masters and a few transactions, the process of importing is the same. Only the excel template is different in which data has to be entered. 
 Data import is normally used by first time users of Farvision, or if there is a huge volume. Bulk data can be inserted into Farvision and it saves time. Once your backlog is cleared, it is recommended to use the interface for day to day entry. Sometimes data import is also used where the number of rows in a document is very large, example a journal voucher with 200 lines. 
 There are four steps to be followed 
 ● Download Template 
 ● Upload Template 
 ● Validate Data 
 ● Import Data 
 DOWNLOAD TEMPLATE 
 Object: This is the master or transaction form for which the excel template has to be downloaded. 
 Nested Objects: Some forms which have to be imported have a lot of data, and have multiple excel worksheets in one excel template. These multiple worksheets normally correspond to tabs of the entry interface. Example, Account Head Import will have the worksheets for Ledger, Ledger Address, Ledger Communication, Ledger Contact, Bank Details, etc. 
 All these worksheets are linked to each other through a common field called Link Ref Code . The same value of this field in each row has to be entered under ImportLinkRefCode in the nested worksheets. In the Ledger worksheet Link Ref Code ‘1’ has details of Amar Singh, Link Ref Code ‘2’ has details of Amit Kumar Pal. In the Ledger Address worksheet, ImportLinkRefCode ‘1’ will contain address details of Amar Singh, Link Ref Code ‘2’ will contain address details of Amit Kumar Pal. The value given to the Link Ref Code and ImportLinkRefCode has to be the same so that data in the different worksheets can be associated with each other. 
 Download template : Download the template by clicking the Download button. An excel file will be downloaded on your local computer. Open the excel sheet. Enter the data in the excel sheet. 
 About the Excel Template 
 There may be one or more worksheets in which data has to or can be entered. Click on the different worksheets to enter data in them. Remember to use the same identifying value in all worksheets so that data between the different worksheets can be linked to each other. In case there is no data to be filled in the nested worksheets, leave it blank. Do not fill only the ImportLinkRefCode if no other data is available for entry in that sheet. In case there is a row in the main sheet but there is no associated data for that row in the linked sheets, skip that row number in the linked sheet. 
 Each excel template has an Info worksheet which will guide the user about the properties of the fields. 
 Sheet Name : Worksheet names are listed here. 
 Column Names : Fields available in all associated worksheets are listed here. Data has to be entered as rows, fields are the columns. 
 Properties : Fields can have the following properties 
 Is required: True - this is a mandatory field, has to be entered. 
 Is required: False - this is an optional field. 
 Max length: The maximum number of characters which can be entered in that field. 
 The following points have to be kept in mind while filling data in the prescribed excel sheet 
 Do not remove any columns or worksheets , even if there is no data to be entered in them. Format must be as per the original excel template downloaded. 
 Do not change any names, settings, alignment, formatting of fields, worksheet, or files . 
 Remove any hyperlinks from the data fields . Example Email. 
 Try to import records into batches of 100, 200 or 500 rows at a time. Import can be run multiple times. Data will keep on getting added in Farvision. 
 Fill all mandatory fields 
 Enter data in ImportLinkRefCode if data is there in the associated worksheets 
 Do not enter blank rows , especially at the end of the excel sheet 
 Wherever applicable, Debit and Credit amounts should tally . 
 Spelling of account heads, parent account, items, etc should be correct, i.e. match with the masters in Farvision 
 Wherever applicable, data in related sheets should tally with the data in the main sheet . Example, Receipt/Payment or Journals, the Adjustment Info amount for each party should tally with the amount in Ledger details for the same party. 
 Some tips 
 Clear cache and clear history of the browser, in case of unknown error 
 UPLOAD TEMPLATE 
 Upload the filled out excel Template to start the data uploading process. 
 Select File : Select the file in which data has been entered and has to be uploaded. 
 The template can be dragged and dropped or the same can be selected from its location. Click on the Drop files to upload panel. Select the file in which data has been entered and has to be uploaded. Click on the Upload button. Once the template has been uploaded, it will show the message Uploaded Successfully. Click on Next button to go to the data validation step. VALIDATE DATA Once the filled up excel has been uploaded, the data has to be validated from the template and click on Next 
 Process Queue : Click on the box so that the validation process can be routed through the Queue Management console. If the data volume is large, it is important to queue this process else the server will become very slow. 
 Validate Data : Click on the Start Validation button to start the validation process. 
 Status : While the data validation is ongoing, a status bar will show Validating Data, Please Wait. If the data validation is successful, it will show the status as Success. If data is not correct and has failed the validation process, it will show Error Found. 
 Result : In case the status is not successful, the reasons why validation has failed will be provided in this Excel file which can be downloaded. The file will have both data which has a problem and data which is correct. The data where there is a problem is highlighted in yellow. The problems with the data will be displayed in the Import Remarks column. In this example, HSN Id does not exist for Construction service in HSN Master. 
 In this example, Relationship should have Son or Wife, and the name Rakesh Kumar and Mahaveer Singh should have been entered in Relative Name respectively. 
 In this example, Postal code is a mandatory field that can’t be blank. 
 The validation routine has to be run repeatedly till there are no errors left. 
 Click on the Next button to go to the Import Data tab. 
 IMPORT DATA 
 Click on Start Import to start importing data from filled up excel template file into Farvision. On successful import, it will show the status as Success. Click on the Finish button. Data which has been imported can be checked in the respective Advanced Search for the transaction or master forms. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Discussion for Cut off and opening balance [method to follow]
text:
Discussion for Cut off and opening balance [method to follow] 
 Knowledge Base" />
 Knowledge 
 Base 
 HOW TO TAKE 
 ACCOUNTING CUT OFF AND DO BALANCE CARRY FORWARD FOR FIRST YEAR OF ERP 
 IMPLEMENTATION? 
 Method 
 1 
 [Strongly Recommended] 
 Process 
 A 
 cut off should be taken on discussed and specified date. 
 Closing 
 balance should be taken from the legacy accounting system and import 
 the opening balance in Farvision ERP on the discussed and specified 
 cut-off date. 
 P&L 
 opening balance also needs to be imported. 
 Hence 
 there will be no backlog data. 
 The 
 old legacy data can be attached ledger wise in PDF format in the Farvision 
 ERP. 
 Cut-off 
 date must be first day of any month. 
 Success 
 rate is 100%. 
 Concern (s) 
 · Clients may 
 raise a concern that in the mid of the year if they migrate from any legacy 
 system to Farvision, they may face audit challenges AND they need to 
 maintain both the system for the first financial year. 
 Answer - For listed companies, customers may need 
 to keep a resolution from Audit team for this process. 
 Method 
 2 
 Import legacy 
 accounting system data [only financial accounting data] AS IT IS to Farvision 
 via excel template 
 Process 
 User 
 can download Receipt, Payment, Journal, Contra, NSP excel import template 
 from Farvision ERP system. 
 User can arrange the legacy accounting 
 system data in Farvision ERP specified import template. 
 And 
 import the data in Farvision ERP. 
 The 
 data should be before cut-off date. 
 Client 
 audit team MUST audit the data before and after import 
 Legacy accounting 
 system must be locked for the period data, which data to be imported, 
 as no data can be edited or deleted in the legacy system, once the 
 import decision finalized and work started. 
 Concern (s) 
 a. Till backlog 
 data will not be completed today’s entry SHALL not be started. 
 1. If user start today’s entry, the bill wise 
 outstanding and bill wise adjustment needs to reconciled and corrected 
 at later stage. 
 2. The TDS must be reconciliated later stage 
 3. User needs to careful for payment 
 4. Different type of documents for accounts series 
 in same financial year needs to be created for current transaction and 
 Back-Log data. 
 5. Till time back-log data will not be completed 
 GST and related ITC reconciliation will not be processed. 
 b. Issue in 
 the time line, project handover and closure time line may be extended 
 if the import and golive transactional process not completed according 
 to the schedule. Even if number of data can be a challenge. 
 c. Ledger and 
 Chart of account structural issue, the same structure of legacy system 
 needs to imported / created in Farvision ERP for smooth data import. But 
 below ledger dimension is ERP specific only like 
 1. Control 
 account 
 2. Same As 
 3. Free Subledger 
 d. Henceforth 
 legacy system’s duplicate ledger may need to be created in Farvision ERP 
 only for import purpose. Like in Contractor accounting and related mobilization, 
 secure advance as well as retention money. 
 e. Statutory 
 automation will not work. AND after import statutory manual ledger of 
 legacy system MUST be reconciled and discontinued. Statutory means TDS 
 , GST , TCS etc. 
 f. Sales and Customer care accounts data 
 import process needs to discuss separately. 
 g. As ERP has 
 only one cut off date hence Stock opening and fixed asset process needs 
 to be discussed separately. 
 h. As ERP has 
 only one cut off date hence Budget and Work order as well as RA bill opening 
 process needs to be discussed separately. 
 i. Profit and loss need to be audited and reconciled. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

text:
Chart Of Account Master 
 Help > Setup > Ledger" />
 Chart of Account 
 Master 
 A chart of account (COA) 
 is a list of the accounts created and used by an organization 
 to define each class of items for which money or the equivalent is spent 
 or received. 
 It is used to organize the 
 accounts and to segregate expenditures, revenue, assets and liabilities. 
 ‘Chart of 
 Account Master’ interface is used to create new chart of account. Each 
 chart of account will have a unique code and description. 
 Code : 
 Chart Of Account code is to be provided here. 
 Description : 
 Description of 'Cart Of Account' is to be provided here. 
 Is 
 Primary : Check this if the 'Chart Of Account' is to be used as 
 primary. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Group Master
text:
Group Master 
 Help > Setup > Ledger" />
 Tutorial: Creating Group Master 
 Group 
 Master 
 The ‘Account Group Master’ allows to arrange account 
 heads under several account groups. It lists four primary account groups 
 described as – Equity and Liabilities, Assets, Revenue and then Expenses 
 – are by default and fixed. However, further grouping of accounts can 
 also be made to create a tree structure under the primary account groups. 
 Template : 
 Select any pre-built template 
 COA (Chart of Accounts) : Select chart of accounts where groups of 
 account heads are structured in form of a tree. Each parent group can 
 further be sub divided into more than one sub-groups. 
 In 
 the upper part of the window there are ‘Group Master’ drop-down menu including 
 ‘New (Add Group)’ and ‘Delete (Delete Group)’. They are used to make an 
 addition of new account group (Add Group) and delete a group from the 
 Chart of accounts (Delete Group). 
 The 
 upper left hand side of the window displays the names of account heads . 
 Description 
 Clicking 
 on any account group will display its description in right panel 
 Add 
 Group 
 To 
 add a new group, click ‘Group Master’ drop down menu and then click ‘New’. 
 A small dialogue box named ‘Add Group’ will appear on the screen where 
 you need to select parent group and then specify the name of the account 
 group in ‘Enter Group Description’ textbox. 
 Select 
 the parent group. The new account group will come under this Account Group. 
 Finally, 
 click ‘Save’ button to add the new account group under the selected parent 
 account group. 
 After successful 
 creation of the group, the following message will be evoked and under 
 the parent group the new group will be visible. 
 Delete 
 Group 
 To 
 delete a group, click ‘Group Master’ drop down menu and then click ‘Delete’ 
 to delete an account group. A new window named ‘Delete Group’ opens. To 
 delete an account group, first, select the particular account group and 
 then click ‘Save’ button. It is to be noted that if an account group already 
 contains account head(s), that group cannot be deleted. 
 Filter Options 
 1. Update Group 
 Click on the Update Group option 
 The grid will open with all Account Heads and 
 Groups 
 Click on the grid which needs to be updated. 
 Now the pop up will open for ‘Update Group’ 
 . 
 Here choose the Schedule for the group and click 
 on "Update". 
 2. Rename Group 
 Click on the Rename Group option. In Rename 
 Group pop up select the group which needs to be renamed. 
 Click on ‘Rename’ after changing the group name 
 in Rename Group text field. 
 Restriction 
 on Group Master Rename 
 System Generated Group Name cannot be changed 
 3. Transfer Head 
 The 
 ‘Transfer Head’ allows transferring ledgers from one group to another 
 group 
 This 
 menu can be seen under Group Master Menu. 
 After 
 clicking on the Transfer Head, Groups will be shown. Click on the group 
 from which ledger needs to be transferred 
 After 
 that choose the ledger, which needs to be transferred. Click Save. 
 A 
 popup window will open. Select the group where ledger will be transferred. 
 Click Save. 
 4. Mapping Account Head 
 The 
 ‘Mapping Account Head’ is used to tag ledgers with new/existing template 
 master. 
 After 
 clicking on the Mapping Account Head, ledger will be shown which is to 
 be tagged for default template (if any). Select the Template and 
 corresponding COA for which mapping will be done. 
 Click 
 on the ledger grid which needs to be mapped. A popup window will open. 
 Here group needs to be selected. After selection click Save. 
 5. Transfer Sub Group 
 User 
 can transfer a sub group from one group to another group. User Can transfer 
 the Sub Group when Ledger exists in Source Group but not in Target Group. 
 Note : Only leaf groups (I.E. last level 
 group) can be transferred 
 Tutorial: 
 Creating Group Master 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Account Head Master

 Tutorial: Creating Account Head Master

 Master 
 Account head or ledger is essential for any accounting

 code

 type

 FCNR stands for Foreign Currency Non Resident and FCBU stands for Foreign

 address type. The two address types are Permanent and Correspondence

 address

 Enter name of the country

 be auto populated

 will be auto populated

 Enter the date from when this address is effective. 
 Phone : Enter 
 phone number

 Click ‘Save’ button. 
 C. Bank Account Details 
 Click ' Add 
 New Row ' 
 Beneficiary

 Enter beneficiary bank account number 
 Beneficiary Bank A/C Name : Enter beneficiary bank account name 
 IFSC/IBAN No. : 
 Enter IFSC or IBAN number as required 
 Bank Address : 
 Enter bank address 
 Swift 
 Code : Provide Swift code if any 
 Account Type: Enter 
 Account Type 
 Beneficiary Bank Name : 
 Enter the beneficiary bank name 
 Branch Code : 
 Enter the branch code 
 IsDefault : This 
 is selected if the bank account detail is taken as default 
 Click 
 'Save' button. 
 D. Contact Person Info 
 Type: 
 Select the type as permanent 
 or temporary 
 Name: 
 Enter name of the contact person 
 Designation/Profile: 
 Enter the designation of the contact 
 person 
 Email: 
 Enter the email address of the contact 
 person 
 Owner 
 Name: Name of the owner can be entered 
 Category: 
 Select the category among Billing, 
 Owner, Management and FV Payment Portal 
 Phone: 
 Enter the phone number of the contact 
 person 
 Mobile: 
 Enter the mobile number of the contact 
 person 
 Active 
 From: Active From date can be entered 
 Active 
 To: Active To date can be entered 
 Is 
 Default: Select this option if 
 the contact person is required to be 
 set as default 
 2. Account Head 
 Type 'General Ledger' 
 Account Head Address 
 Enter account 
 head address details as discussed above 
 3. Account Head 
 Type 'Cash' 
 Account Head Address 
 Enter account 
 head address details as discussed above 
 4. Account Head Type 'Control Account' 
 Control Account Info 
 Classification : Select 
 classification of the control account from drop down list 
 Free Sub Ledger : A 
 control account which is by default become the parent ledger of any sub 
 account head 
 Same As : If 
 any parent account head (Normal type) is linked with same as option with 
 another parent account head (supplier, customer or normal type) then the 
 sub account heads of the parent ledger are also get tagged with the parent 
 ledger selected in same as option. 
 Click 'Submit' 
 button 
 5. Account Head Type 'Sub Ledger' 
 A. Parent Info 
 Control 
 Account : Select the control 
 account 
 Classification : the classification of control account 
 will be populated 
 Is Parent 
 Company : 
 This is selected if this is a Parent Company 
 Parent Company : 
 Search or enter name of the parent company

 This is selected if this is a Consignee 
 Sub-Contractor : 
 This is selected if this is a Sub-Contractor 
 B. 
 Account Head Address 
 Provide account head address details 
 as discussed above 
 C. 
 Bank Account Details 
 Provide bank account details as 
 discussed above 
 D. 
 TDS Info 
 PAN : Enter PAN 
 TDS Type : Three 
 types of TDS available such as 'Deduction', 'No TDS' and 'TDS Applicable 
 But Exempted'. Select as per requirement 
 i. Deduction 
 If 'TDS Type' 
 is deduction then 'Company Type' should be selected 
 Company 
 Type : Select Company or Other Than Company whichever is applicable 
 ii. No TDS

 iii. TDS Applicable

 If TDS Type 
 is 'TDS Applicable But Exempted' then 'Company Type' should be selected 
 E. 
 TDS Ledger Tag

 At First user has to create a ledger

 Step1: Go to Setup > Ledger

 Step3: Go to tool tip > click

 Step4: Go to TDS Ledger Tagging 
 TAB

 Existing Nature

 from there

 Then Click on Discontinue > Check box will be dimmed

 Now the discontinued natures will

 If user wants to delete the nature 
 Step9: Go to Finance Module

 Find the ledger

 of Existing Nature 
 Step14: Two options will be available 
 from there 
 (If

 Deleted nature will not be appearing

 6. Account Head 
 Type 'Parent Company' 
 Account Head 
 Address

 head address details as discussed above

 time changes required for Account Head Master (those not using this preference

title: Sub Ledger Group(Category)
text:
Sub Ledger Group(Category) 
 Help > Setup > Ledger" />
 Sub Ledger Group (Category) 
 This sub-ledger group is used to categorise customer 
 and supplier data. For example, the user can categorise suppliers as cement 
 suppliers or steel suppliers. This is how we use this interface. 
 Note that this categorisation is not limited to suppliers; 
 it can also be applied to customer data. 
 Essentially, when creating a ledger or account head, 
 we tag it with this sub-ledger group to ensure proper categorisation. 
 Steps to Create Sub Ledger Group (Category) 
 Navigate to Financial> Setup> 
 Ledger> Sub Ledger Group (Category). 
 Enter the code and description. 
 After filling in the details, click 
 on Submit to save the entry. 
 Now, we will implement 
 this Category to an Account Head. 
 For this, navigate 
 to Financials> Setup> Ledger> Account Head Master. 
 Enter the code 
 (non-mandatory field), description, alternate description (non-mandatory 
 field), as applicable. 
 Under Account 
 Type, choose Sub Ledger, after which the following screen can be seen. 
 Click on ‘Sub 
 Ledger Classification and Credit Control’ field. 
 The following 
 screen will open from where the user can tag the category accordingly. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Ledger Control Account Transfer
text:
Ledger Control Account Transfer 
 Help > Setup > Ledger" />
 Ledger 
 Control Account Transfer 
 S ometimes 
 Account head grouping needs to be changed in the Chart of Accounts. Transfer 
 Head option in the task bar allows all or selected ledgers from one group 
 to be transferred to another group. 
 Select 
 the required account group from where the account heads have to be transferred. 
 Select the account heads under that group which need to be transferred 
 to another group and click on the 'Save' button. 
 Example, 
 Loan against Land Purchase needs to be transferred from Other Current 
 Assets to Current 
 Liabilities > Secured Loans. 
 Another window will open where user can select 
 the account groups to which the earlier selected accounts heads have to 
 be moved. 
 Click on the 'Save' button. Account head has been 
 transferred to another group now. 
 Ledger will not show to transfer due to the following 
 reasons 
 1. Same as 
 Ledger cannot be transferred. Parent same as ledger also cannot be transferred. 
 2. Free sub 
 ledger Control Account transfer not possible. 
 3. Transfer 
 can be done from only Normal type of ledger to only Normal type of ledger. 
 4. Transfer 
 can be done from only Supplier type of ledger to only Supplier type of 
 ledger. 
 5. Transfer 
 can be done from only Customer type to only Customer type of ledger. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

 Enter the code, description, country,

 Once done, click on Submit to save the

 Now, we will implement this Sub State 
 to an Account Head. 
 For this, navigate to Financials> 
 Setup> Ledger> Account Head Master. 
 Enter the code (non-mandatory field), 
 description, alternate description (non-mandatory field), as applicable. 
 Under Account Type, choose Sub Ledger, 
 after which the following screen can be seen. 
 Click on ‘Sub Ledger Classification 
 and Credit Control’ field. 
 The following screen will open from 
 where the user can tag the sub-state accordingly.

 HSN

 Harmonised 
 system of nomenclature (HSN) is an internationally accepted coding system 
 for product and service to maintain uniformity in classification of goods 
 and services. 
 HSN : Put or search the required 
 HSN code in ‘HSN’ field 
 Description : Description 
 of HSN should be provided here 
 Goods/Service : Select ‘Goods’ 
 or ‘Services’ from drop down 
 Type : There are four types 
 available such as Taxable, Non GST, NIL and Exempted. These ‘types’ are 
 very useful for return submission. Select 
 as per the requirement. 
 Reverse Charge : Check if 
 applicable 
 CGST : Put the CGST rate 
 as applicable 
 SGST : SGST will be auto 
 filled up

 filled up 
 Outside State Eligibility : 
 This box is enabled to be checked to receive services from unregistered 
 parties which are from outside the state. For unregistered parties outside 
 the state, only services are allowed. 
 Abatement : 
 This is for providing abatement ratio factor. 
 Based 
 On: There are two options – Quantity and Value 
 1. 
 Value 
 based option : 
 Tax 
 amount gets calculated on the basis of percentage 
 or rate of the 
 taxable value of the goods/services 
 2. 
 Quantity 
 based option : 
 It 
 is used only where ‘CESS’ 
 is applicable, where 
 CESS amount gets calculated on the basis of physical quantity of goods 
 (like coal product, tobacco product etc.) 
 CESS : Enter 
 CESS rate depending on value or quantity, if applicable 
 * Discontinued : Check 
 this box if the particular HSN is not required or no longer to be used. 
 Once it is discontinued can not be continued again.

title: Overview of Public and Private Keys in SSL certificate
text:
Overview of Public and Private Keys in SSL certificate 
 Help > Setup > E-Banking > E-Banking Setup > Outward Remittance > Public and Private keys in SSL certificate" />
 Overview 
 of Public and Private Keys in SSL certificate 
 Data transferred between E-banking portal 
 and Farvision has to be encrypted as per norms of the bank with which 
 integration is being done. Each client needs a public and private key 
 for this purpose. The client has to arrange for a SSL certificate which 
 will contain the public and private key. When Farvision sends data to 
 the bank, Farvision will use the Public key provided by the bank to encrypt 
 the data and bank will use it’s own private key to decrypt the data sent 
 by Farvision. 
 When bank 
 sends data to Farvision, it will use client’s Public key to encrypt the 
 data and Farvision will use client’s private key to decrypt the data sent 
 by the bank. 
 ICICI bank needs a 4096 bit encrypted certificate. 
 The format of the certificate will be Base-64 encoded X.509 (.cer). Once 
 the SSL certificate with the above specifications has been purchased from 
 the Certification Authority (CA), the public key has to be obtained from 
 within the certificate and shared with ICICI bank. It is not mandatory 
 to install the certificate on your website. The certificate is only needed

 The Certificate Signing Request (CSR) file has to

 THE CSR CAN BE GENERATED FROM ANY COMPUTER. THERE 
 IS NO NECESSITY THAT THE CSR BE GENERATED FROM THE SERVER WHERE YOUR DOMAIN 
 OR WEBSITE IS HOSTED. ONLY IMPORTANT POINT IS THAT THE PRIVATE KEY HAS 
 TO BE GENERATED FROM THE SAME COMPUTER AND KEPT SAFELY. THIS PRIVATE KEY

 Start Internet 
 Information Services (IIS) Manager. 
 Select server: Select the server in the Connections pane, on the

 service provider, and a bit length of 4096. When you are finished, click 
 the Next button. 
 Create file 
 name and click “Finish”. 
 Next 
 steps 
 You’re finished!

title: On Account Adjustment IU
text:
On Account Adjustment IU 
 Help > Adjustment" />
 On Account 
 Adjustment IU 
 On Account Adjustment - IU is a financial 
 process used to adjust bills against advances between different business 
 units within the same organisation. This interface allows for the seamless 
 reconciliation of advances given or received by one unit with the bills 
 generated by or for another unit. 
 When is this feature applicable? 
 The concept involves an advance payment 
 made to a business unit under the same contractor. When another business 
 unit starts work under the same contractor and a bill is issued, the developer 
 requests the contractor to adjust the advance payment against the new 
 business unit. 
 Use Case Example 
 In a project with multiple business 
 units, an advance payment was made to one unit, but due to unforeseen 
 circumstances, the work was not executed. Subsequently, another new business 
 unit was assigned under the same contractor. The developer requested the 
 contractor to adjust the previously paid advance amount with the bill 
 generated for the new business unit. 
 The concerned team used the ‘on account 
 adjustment IU’ to adjust the advance amount from the first unit with the 
 bill released for the second unit. This adjustment was recorded in the 
 finance module, ensuring that the financial records accurately reflected 
 the transfer. As a result, the second business unit’s billing was adjusted 
 accordingly, and future payments for the second business unit would be 
 based on the adjusted advance amount. 
 Steps to Implement On Account Adjustment – IU 
 Navigate to Finance> Adjustment> 
 On Account Adjustment – IU. 
 Choose the preferred Business Unit and 
 Financial Year. 
 Under Document Type, select Inter Unit 
 On Account Adjustment. 
 Document No will be auto generated. 
 Tag the preferred Account Head and Select 
 Document, as needed. 
 Under This Adjustment Field, enter the 
 amount which needs to be adjusted. 
 Enter any Prefix or Narration, as required. 
 Once the above fields are filled, click 
 on Add New Row upon which the following window will open. 
 Under Type, choose Bill Wise and tag 
 the bill in the next field. 
 Click on Save once done. 
 Once all of this is done, the screen 
 below will look like the following. 
 Click on Submit to save the entry and 
 On Account Adjustment – IU will be done against the tagged bill. 
 Alternatively, the Tag Bill option can 
 also be used to tag the respective bill directly from the populated list 
 of documents in grid format. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

text:

 Help > Banking" />
 Bank 
 Reconciliation Statement 
 A Bank Reconciliation Statement (BRS) 
 is a document that compares the bank balance on a company’s books of accounts 
 to the corresponding amount on its bank statement. This process helps 
 to reconcile any discrepancies between the two records and ensures that 
 the company’s financial records are accurate. 
 When is it Used? 
 · A BRS is typically used to reconcile 
 the difference in amount of the bank balance as per the cash book against 
 the bank balance as per the bank statement. 
 · It helps by adding those entries in 
 the books of accounts which were done by the banker but were missing in 
 the bank ledger in the books of accounts. 
 · It helps detect errors, such as missed

 Use Case Example

 shows a withdrawal that is not recorded in the company’s books. Upon investigation,

 the company was unaware of. By identifying this discrepancy, the real

 steps to avoid such fees in the future.

 Payment 
 Requisition 
 A 
 payment requisition refers to the formal request made by the Finance, 
 Material, or any other department to their Accounts/Finance Team to make 
 payment to their creditors (supplier, contractor, or any payable account). 
 Benefits of Creating Payment Requisition 
 By 
 documenting and formalising payment requests, the system ensures that 
 all payments are authorised and supported by valid documentation, which 
 helps prevent unauthorised or fraudulent payments. 
 The 
 payment requisition process provides transparency by creating a clear 
 trail of communication and approval for each payment, enhancing accountability 
 and reducing the risk of disputes. 
 Use Case 
 In 
 a real estate development project, a contractor completes a milestone 
 according to the agreed-upon work order. The contractor then submits a 
 payment requisition, attaching relevant documentation such as invoices, 
 timesheets, or completion certificates. The Payment Requisition 
 is routed to the concerned team for review and approval. Once approved, 
 the request is forwarded to the finance department for processing. The 
 finance team verifies the documentation and processes the payment according 
 to the approved amount and schedule.

 after ‘Statutory Info’ details is provided

title: BG Cancellation
text:
BG Cancellation 
 Help > BG/FD" />
 BG Cancellation 
 This interface is only applicable when 
 there are non-expired Bank Guarantees (BG). If any BG has expired, it 
 won’t show in this interface. 
 Steps For BG Cancellation 
 Navigate to 
 Financials> BG/FD> BG Cancellation. 
 The following 
 screen is displayed where all the Bank Guarantee (BG) which have not been 
 expired are displayed. 
 Click on the 
 desired BG, to open the following screen. 
 Enter the following details: 
 · Guarantee 
 Status : Choose ‘cancelled’ 
 from the drop-down. 
 · Closure Type : Specifies the method or reason for 
 the closure of the Bank Guarantee. Two options are available: 
 1. Remitted : This 
 closure type indicates that the bank guarantee is canceled because the 
 required payment or transfer of funds (remittance) has been made. For 
 example, if a bank guarantee was issued to ensure payment for goods or 
 services, once the buyer makes the payment to the seller, the guarantee 
 can be canceled as it has served its purpose. 
 2. Exhausted : This 
 closure type signifies that the full amount covered by the bank guarantee, 
 has been utilised or drawn upon, leaving no remaining funds or obligations 
 under the guarantee. For instance, if a bank guarantee was issued for 
 a certain sum to cover liabilities or payments, and the beneficiary has 
 claimed or received the full guaranteed amount, the guarantee is exhausted 
 and should be canceled. 
 · Cancel Date : The date on which the Bank Guarantee 
 was cancelled. 
 · Remarks/Reason : Additional notes or reasons for the 
 status or closure of the Bank Guarantee. 
 Click on Submit to Cancel the BG. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Bank Guarantee
text:
Bank Guarantee 
 Help > BG/FD" />
 Bank Guarantee 
 A bank guarantee 
 refers to a promise provided by a bank or any other financial institution 
 that if a certain borrower fails to pay a loan, then the bank or the financial 
 institution will take care of the losses. The bank will assure the original 
 creditor through this bank guarantee that if the borrower does not meet 
 his or her liabilities, then the bank will take care of them. 
 The 
 Applicant-(the party that requests a bank guarantee from the bank 
 and borrows from a creditor) 
 The 
 Beneficiary (the party that receives a partial guarantee) 
 The Bank 
 (the party that agrees to sign and assures payment in case the applicant 
 fails to repay the loan) 
 BG 
 RECEIPT: 
 BG 
 ISSUE: 
 Deferred payment guarantee : This 
 refers to a bank guarantee or a payment guarantee that is offered to the 
 exporter for a deferred period or for a certain time period. When a buyer 
 purchases capital goods or machinery, the seller will give credit to the 
 buyer when the buyer’s bank gives a guarantee that it will pay the unsettled 
 dues of the buyer to the seller. Under this type of guarantee, payment 
 will be made in instalments by the bank for failure in supplying raw materials, 
 machinery or equipment. 
 Financial guarantee : A 
 financial bank guarantee assures that money will be repaid if the party 
 does not complete a particular project or operation entirely. According 
 to the financial guarantee agreement, when there is a delay in the completion 
 of the project, the bank will make the payment. 
 Advance payment guarantee : Under 
 this kind of guarantee, an advance payment will be made to the seller. 
 There will also be a guarantee that if the seller fails to deliver the 
 service or product accurately or promptly, the buyer will receive a refund 
 of the payment. 
 Foreign bank guarantee : A 
 foreign bank guarantee is provided by a bank on behalf of a borrower. 
 This will be offered on behalf of the foreign beneficiary or creditor. 
 Performance guarantee : Under 
 a performance guarantee, compensation of money will be made by the bank 
 when there is any delay in delivering the performance or operation. Payment 
 will have to be made even if the service is delivered inadequately. 
 Bid 
 bond guarantee : Under this type of guarantee, there will be a 
 supply bidding procedure. This will be conducted by the contractor for 
 the owner of an infrastructure or industrial project or any kind of operation. 
 The contractor of the project will guarantee that the best bidder or the 
 highest bidder will have the capability and authority to implement a project 
 as per his or her preferences. The bid bond will be given to the owner 
 of the project as a proof of guarantee and the bond will imply that the 
 project will have to be devised according to the bid contract. 
 COMMISSION CHARGES 
 Based 
 on the type of the BG , fees are generally charged on a quarterly 
 basis on the BG value of 0.75% or 0.50% during the BG validity 
 period. Apart from this, the bank may also charge the 
 application processing fee , documentation fee , 
 and handling fee . 
 FDR PROCESS IN LINK WITH BANK GUARANTEE 
 Bank 
 Guarantees are issued against some margin money or at 100% margin 
 which is keep in the form of FDR . Suppose a company need to 
 furnish one time guarantee to some government authority, 
 it will create a FDR (100% margin) and request the bank to issue the BG against 
 such FDR . 
 A sample 
 entry where commission is provided 
 Steps To Create a Bank Guarantee 
 Navigate to Financials> BG/FD> 
 Bank Guarantee. The following screen will be visible. 
 Fill in the details as required. 
 Main Info 
 Business Unit: Choose the preferred 
 Business Unit. 
 Financial Year: Choose the preferred 
 Financial Year. 
 Document Type: Under Document Type, 
 there are two options: 
 Bank 
 Guarantee - (BGF): Applicable while creating a new Bank Guarantee. 
 Bank Guarantee Renewal - (BGRNEW): Applicable 
 when an existing Bank Guarantee needs to be renewed. 
 Document Date: Auto-populates. The user 
 can choose the date according to requirement. 
 Document No: Auto-populates. 
 Basic Info 
 Project Name: Choose the preferred Project 
 Name. 
 Project Status: Under this field, there 
 are four options: 
 New: Applicable for a project that has 
 just started and is in its initial phase. 
 Ongoing: Applicable 
 for an ongoing project. 
 Completed: Applicable for a project 
 that has been finished and all objectives met. 
 Prospect: Applicable for a project that 
 is being considered or planned. 
 Guarantee Category: Under this field, 
 there are three options available: 
 Issue: Applicable for an issued guarantee. 
 Receive: Applicable for a guarantee 
 which is going to be received. 
 On Behalf of (DSR): Applicable to the 
 person or entity on whose behalf the guarantee is being issued. 
 Guarantee Type: There are multiple options 
 available in this field. Choose one which suits the requirement: 
 Performance: Guarantee ensuring the 
 fulfillment of contractual obligations. 
 Bid: Guarantee provided to ensure the 
 bidder’s commitment. 
 Advanced: Guarantee for advance payments 
 made. 
 Normal: Standard guarantee without special 
 conditions. 
 Retention: Guarantee for retaining a 
 portion of payment until project completion. 
 Bid Bond [EMD]: Earnest Money Deposit 
 to secure the bid. 
 Mobilization Advance: Guarantee for 
 advance funds to start a project. 
 FMG Release: Guarantee for the release 
 of Foreign Material Goods. 
 SD Charges: Guarantee for Security Deposit 
 charges. 
 SD Against Material Purchase: Guarantee 
 for Security Deposit against material purchase. 
 Others: Any other type of guarantee 
 not listed above. 
 Guarantee No: Enter a unique number. 
 Guarantee Amount: Enter the amount as 
 required. 
 BG Margin %: Enter any BG Margin %, 
 if applicable. 
 BG Margin Amount: Enter any BG Margin 
 Amount, if applicable. 
 Issue Date: The date on which the bank 
 guarantee is issued. 
 Notification Date: The date on which 
 the beneficiary is notified about the guarantee. 
 Start Date: The date from which the 
 bank guarantee becomes effective. 
 Claim Date: The last date by which a 
 claim can be made under the guarantee. 
 Expiry Date: The date on which the bank 
 guarantee expires. 
 Bank Info 
 Bank Name: Enter the applicable Bank 
 Name. 
 Beneficiary Name: Enter the applicable 
 Beneficiary Name. 
 FDR Detail: Choose the preferred FD 
 against which the BG will be processed. 
 Commission 
 Info 
 BG Receive/Issue: Choose the appliable 
 receiver or issuer for Bank Guarantee. 
 BG Issue Purpose: The reason or purpose 
 for issuing the bank guarantee. Multiple options are available. 
 Commission Type: The type of commission 
 applicable to the bank guarantee. Segregated into 4 options namely monthly, 
 quarterly, half yearly, and yearly. 
 Commission %: The percentage rate of 
 the commission to be given annually. (If the commission type is set 
 to either monthly, quarterly, or half yearly, it will be processed accordingly 
 based on the annual %). 
 No of Installment: The number of installments 
 for commission payment. 
 Tax Amount: The total tax amount applicable 
 to the bank guarantee. 
 Narration: A brief description or note 
 regarding the bank guarantee. 
 Extra Info 
 Other Charges: Additional fees or charges 
 associated with the bank guarantee. 
 License No: The license number related 
 to the bank guarantee. 
 Project Name of Work: The name of the 
 project for which the bank guarantee is issued. 
 Project Address: The address where the 
 project is located. 
 Once the above details are filled, click 
 on Generate to process the Bank Guarantee. 
 Bank Guarantee 
 Renewal 
 Under Document 
 Type, select Bank Guarantee Renewal - (BGRNEW). 
 Renewal Info 
 BG Ref 
 No: Select the BG which 
 needs to be renewed. 
 Renewal 
 Reason: Enter the reason 
 for renewal. 
 Basic Info 
 Under Basic Info, the user can change 
 the Start Date, Claim Date, and Expiry Date. 
 The rest of the fields are auto populated. 
 Commission 
 Info 
 In this screen, the user can change 
 the Commission Type, Commission %, No of Installment, Tax Amount, Narration, 
 and BG Issue Purpose. 
 Once all the details are filled, click 
 on Generate to process the Renewed BG.

 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Farvision E-Invoice System Process Flow
text:
Farvision E-Invoice System Process Flow 
 Help > E-Invoicing" />
 Farvision 
 E-Invoice System Process Flow 
 Farvision E-Invoice System (FVEIS) 
 provides 
 end-to-end solution for E-Invoice to FV-GST Portal users: 
 Business house 
 will generate invoice as per their business needs and standards. On 
 saving of the invoice or after approval, Invoices are kept in a queue 
 to be sent for processing GSTN- Invoice Registration Portal (IRP). 
 The sending of the invoices is as per an internal backend scheduler 
 of Farvision, which runs every 15 minutes, or as configured by us. 
 FVEIS will upload multiple invoices in bulk and will expose to IRP 
 one by one for each invoice. 
 FVEIS will convert these invoice data into 
 prescribed e-invoice data formats and will be available after a few 
 minutes (as per scheduler timing). It will also provide facility to 
 download the IRN and QR Code from IRP to equip the business house 
 to print its standard invoice with QR code User has to take print 
 out of the invoices as he normally does 
 In Farvision r2, a console 
 has been provided which will display status of e-invoice. Successful, 
 failed (with reason), re-try and print. E-Invoices which are successful 
 can be printed from this console or through advanced search or entry 
 interface. 
 The flow 
 of data is shown in the diagram: 
 E-Invoice components 
 Invoice Registration 
 Number (IRN) 
 P arameters which 
 will be used to generate IRN (hash)are: 
 a. Supplier GSTIN 
 b. Supplier’s invoice number 
 c. Financial year (YYYY-YY) 
 QR Code 
 The QR code will consist of the following e-invoice 
 parameters: 
 a. GSTIN of supplier 
 b. GSTIN of Recipient 
 c. Invoice number as given by 
 Supplier 
 d. Date of generation of invoice 
 e. Invoice value (taxable value 
 and gross tax) 
 f. Number of line items. 
 g. HSN Code of main item (the 
 line item having highest taxable value) 
 h. Unique 
 Invoice Reference Number (IRN) 
 Modules 
 from 
 where e-invoice can be generated in Farvision ERP 
 Following 
 Farvision modules will have the impact of e-Invoice: 
 a. Facility Management (Rental) 
 b. Sales (Real Estate) 
 c. Sales (Commercial) 
 d. Construction (RA Bill to Customer) 
 Documents presently 
 covered under B2B e-invoicing: 
 a: Invoice 
 b: Debit Note 
 c: 
 Credit Note 
 Sequence of activities 
 a. Registration in govt e-invoice 
 portal for user login credentials. 
 b. Check whether your GSTN is 
 e-invoice is auto-enabled. If not, then manually enable it. 
 c. Enable API in Govt e-invoice 
 portal. Share username and password with Farvision team so that Farvision 
 API can communicate with the govt e-invoice portal. 
 d. Invoice generation of the organization 
 would be as per ERP transaction forms of the respective modules. 
 e. Once Invoice gets generated 
 Farvision E-Invoice System (FVEIS) will capture all relevant data for 
 GST e-Invoice. 
 f. FVEIS will upload these data 
 invoice wise for E-Invoice to GST – IRP. 
 g. GST-IRP will generate E-Invoice. 
 Corresponding IRN and QR-Code for each invoice will be generated. 
 h. FVEIS will capture IRN and 
 QR code from GST-IRP and will store those into FV database against each 
 Standard Invoice of the organization. 
 i. The Invoice of the organization 
 will now contain IRN and QR code. This invoice can now be printed from 
 Farvision. 
 j. Checking 
 QR Code of the invoice 
 o Scan the QR code of the printed e-invoice 
 by downloading mobile app. 
 o Download QR Code Verification App Through E-invoicing portal > 
 help > tools > 
 verify QR 
 code App. 
 o After OTP verification you will get a 
 link to download required App for mobile. 
 o Download and install the App for further 
 scan/verifications. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: E-Invoicing: A few Relevant Points
text:
E-Invoicing: A few Relevant Points 
 Help > E-Invoicing" />
 E-Invoicing: 
 A few Relevant Points 
 Basic 
 Understanding: From 
 the Farvision users’ perspective there is NO change in the transaction 
 process through which invoices are getting generated. FVEIS executes all 
 required processes to complete e-invoicing. It is important to note that 
 ‘e-invoice’ in ‘e-invoicing’ doesn’t mean generation of invoice by the 
 Government portal. 
 Transactions: 
 Users 
 of relevant modules will continue to create GST invoices through their 
 own processes in Farvision. FVEIS will upload data of these invoices to 
 ‘Invoice Registration Portal (IRP)’and will download the e-invoice with 
 a unique ‘Invoice Reference Number (IRN)’ and a QR Code. These IRN and 
 QR code will be stored in Farvision. 
 All 
 these processes will be executed through AUTO scheduler. The scheduler 
 will capture invoices from all modules in bulk and will upload one by 
 one to IRP and will download the IRN & QR code for each invoice. This will run at a regular 
 interval (say every 15 minutes). 
 Changes in 
 GST invoice : On the existing GST invoice of the company the above 
 mentioned IRN and QR code can be printed from respective modules. Thus, 
 there is no change in format, logo and all other contents of the prevailing 
 invoices of the company. On the same invoice IRN and QR code will be printed 
 at any suitable position of it. 
 Hence, in all 
 the formats of Invoice, Debit Note and Credit Note the position of QR 
 code needs to be incorporated 
 It is important 
 to note that the printing of IRN on Tax Invoice is optional, as per the 
 FAQ of e-Invoice released by CBIC. Hence, only QR code is mandatory. 
 Documents presently 
 NOT covered under e -invoicing 
 1: 
 Invoice –B2C (Farvision is equipped) 
 2: 
 Invoice with Exempted Items (Bill of Supply) 
 3: 
 Self Invoice raised by Registered Recipient for supplies provided by Transporters, 
 Lawyers, Security Service Providers etc. 
 Linkage 
 with GST Return: Once the e-Invoice gets generated the 
 invoice data gets recorded in GST System. The GST system will auto-populate 
 these data into GSTR-1 of the supplier and GSTR-2A of respective receivers. 
 QR code on 
 B2C invoices: Presently , u ploading of 
 B2C invoices to IRP for e-Invoice is not allowed. There is a separate 
 notification issued by the government for imprinting dynamic QR code on 
 B2C invoices. The purpose of this is to enable digital payment by consumers. 
 This is NO way related to e-invoicing. 
 Rejection 
 of Invoice: If 
 the same invoice has already 
 been uploaded to IRP earlier, it will be rejected by IRP. Farvision checks 
 whether a IRN is already present for an invoice or not. If IRN is already 
 generated. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Cancellation or deletion of invoice
text:
Cancellation or deletion of invoice 
 Help > E-Invoicing" />
 Cancellation 
 or deletion of invoice 
 a) Cancellation 
 of invoice can be done on IRP within 24 hours. Cancellation after 24 hours 
 is not possible nor allowed by govt. on IRP and Farvision ensures this. 
 Moreover, Farvision validates this when any deletion of Invoice is attempted 
 by the users. 
 b) If 
 any document has been deleted within 24 hours after generation of QR 
 Code/IRN, then a cancellation request is automatically sent by Farvision 
 to govt portal for marking the e-invoice as cancelled. Cancellation date 
 is returned by the govt portal. Cancellation status is updated in the 
 govt site and can be checked from there also. 
 c) It is important to note that 
 once an IRN is cancelled, the concerned invoice number cannot be used 
 again. 
 d) Cancellation 
 will be rejected if there is an existing valid e-waybill against the e-invoice. 
 Unless e-waybill is cancelled, invoice cannot be cancelled. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Calculation logic of e-invoice values
text:
Calculation logic of e-invoice values 
 Help > E-Invoicing" />
 Calculation 
 logic of e-invoice values 
 The 
 following details have been provided by the govt. This section is for 
 reference of understanding calculations. All calculations are done automatically 
 through Farvision. 
 Please 
 ensure that the below protocol is followed entry of the e-invoice else 
 it will fail. 
 Validations are done by the govt 
 at two levels 
 1. Item level (goods or 
 service) 
 2. Bill total 
 Item 
 level validation for Goods only 
 Hsn, 
 Uqc(Unit of Measurement), UnitPrice, TotAmt, AssAmt, GstRt, TotItemVal 
 TotAmt = Quantity * UnitPrice 
 The 
 following totaling validations are to be done for items 
 a.Taxable 
 Value of Item = Gross Amount of Item - Discount 
 b. 
 SGST Value of Item = Taxable Value of Item X GST Rate / 2, if intra-state 
 CGST Value of Item = Taxable Value of Item X GST Rate / 2, if intra-state 
 c. 
 IGST Value of Item = Taxable Value of Item X GST Rate, if inter-state 
 d. 
 Cess Value of Item = Taxable Value of Item X Cess Rate 
 e. 
 State Cess Value of Item = Taxable Value of Item X State Cess Rate 
 f. 
 Total Value 
 of Item = Taxable Value of Item + SGST Value of Item + CGST Value of Item 
 + IGST Value of Item + Cess Value of Item + State Cess Value of Item + 
 Non-AdvolCess Value of Item + State Cess Non-advol value of Item + Other 
 charges. 
 (Note: 
 Temporarily, the validation of 'Gross Amount of Item with Quantity and 
 Selling Unit Price' has been withdrawn. 
 g. 
 in case of EXPWOP and SEZWOP, Passed IGST Value of Item will not be validated 
 even actual tax rate is passed, if the passed value of IGST for that is 
 ZERO.) 
 For 
 Service Only 
 Hsn, 
 UnitPrice, TotAmt, AssAmt, GstRt, TotItemVal 
 TotAmt 
 = Quantity * UnitPrice 
 Quantity 
 is not mandatory in case of service; hence the TotalAmt&UnitPrice 
 can be the same. 
 TotAmt 
 -> Basic Value 
 AssAmt 
 -> Assessable Amount for calculating GST 
 GstRt -> 
 The GST Rate (CGST + SGST rate or the IGST rate as applicable) 
 TotItemVal 
 -> The total value of the item 
 Validation 
 for Invoice total value 
 The 
 following validations are to be done on Invoice total 
 a. 
 Total Taxable Value = Taxable Value of all Items 
 b. 
 Total SGST Value = SGST Value of all Items 
 c. 
 Total CGST Value = CGST Value of all Items 
 d. 
 Total IGST Value = IGST Value of all Items 
 e. 
 Total Cess Value = Cess Value of all Items + Non-AdvolCess Value of all 
 Items 
 f. Total State Cess Value = State 
 Cess Value of all Items + State Cess Non-advol Value of all Items 
 g. In case of CREDIT 
 NOTE AND DEBIT NOTE, the ‘IGST/CGST/SGST/CESS value of item’ is not validated 
 with corresponding tax rates and taxable values. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: ITC Reversal Posting
text:
ITC Reversal Posting 
 Help > Taxation" />
 ITC Reversal 
 Posting 
 Input 
 Tax Credit (ITC) Reversal is where users have earlier claimed input and 
 not yet paid the Bill amount (Full/Partial) to Creditor. 
 As 
 per GST rule where Creditor is unpaid more than 180 days then the input 
 claimed earlier will be reversed. 
 This 
 will be tracked against Bill and users need to pass the reversal entry 
 in system to incorporate the same. 
 To 
 implement the above practice this is very difficult to keep track of outstanding 
 Bill wise where 180 days passed or not. To overcome this scenario, we 
 have given a facility to check the same. 
 Under 
 Taxation Section we introduced a Menu named ITC Reversal Posting. 
 Here 
 users can perform: 
 ITC Reversal 
 ITC Re-available 
 ITC Reversal 
 Here 
 system will check GSTIN wise and Business Unit wise Creditor Outstanding. 
 System 
 will check bill wise (Full/Partial) which exceeds 180 days from due date. 
 We 
 also provide facility of generating report before passing transaction 
 from the same window to cross check whether any payment done but kept 
 on account and still not adjusted against bill. 
 On clicking ‘Excel’ user can get 
 the output in excel format as shown below: 
 Here 
 system will provide users an idea of how much ITC will be reversed in 
 respect of CGST, SGST and IGST before proceeding. 
 After 
 checking of data, users need to click on Process button to generate ITC 
 Reversal on the specified date. 
 Next, 
 users can check the transaction passed by system in Journal menu and cross 
 check with the report generated. 
 This 
 entry will also be reflected in GST Report as shown below: 
 ITC Re-available 
 Input 
 Tax Credit (ITC) Re-available is where users have reversed ITC earlier 
 and made creditor payment again and users can re-claim ITC on proportionate 
 basis. 
 This 
 will be tracked against bill which remains unpaid over 180 days and Input 
 duly reversed and users made the creditor payment after reversal then 
 they can re-claim Input. 
 On clicking 
 ITC Reversal users get the option of ITC Re-available and after selection 
 of GSTIN users can be able to get the data against which they are going 
 to re-claim Input.

title: E-TDS/E-TCS
text:
E-TDS/E-TCS 
 Help > Taxation" />
 E-TDS/E-TCS 
 E-TDS is the electronic filing of Returns of 
 Tax Deducted at Source. It is mandatory (w.e.f. June1, 2003) for both 
 government deductors and corporate deductors to furnish their TDS returns 
 in electronic form (e-TDS return). 
 As per the income tax laws, entities (both corporate 
 and non-corporate deductors) making payments to third parties (deductees) 
 need to deduct tax Deductions at source (TDS) from these payments and 
 deposit the same at any of the designated branches of authorized banks. 
 They also need to furnish TDS returns containing details of deductee(s) 
 and bank where TDS amount is deposited with the Income Tax Department 
 (ITD). 
 How 
 do you fill up E-TDS? 
 The 
 'E-TDS interface is used to carry out all the necessary entries regarding 
 Electronic -Tax Deductions at Source. 
 The 
 'E-TDS' interface consists of two tabs, including General Info and Responsible 
 Person Info. 
 The 
 items in ' General Info ' tab 
 are necessary to accept information primarily on challan details and quarter(s) 
 of a financial year. 
 The 
 items in ' Responsible Person 
 Info ' tab are necessary to accept information primarily on personal 
 details of the taxpayer. 
 General 
 Info 
 After 
 selecting company name from Company 
 drop-down list, click on the General 
 Info tab. 
 In the General Info tab fill up the required fields 
 as described below 
 Date 
 of Creation: Select the date of entry from the calendar popup 
 Financial 
 Year: User doesn't need to fill-up this field. It will automatically 
 be updated 
 Assessment Year: 
 User doesn't need to fill-up this field. It will automatically be updated 
 Quarter: 
 Select any of the Quarters (01/02/03/04) of the financial year. A year 
 generally consists of four quarters. From four quarters, the Q1 indicates 
 the first quarter (from 1 st April to 30 th June), 
 Q2 indicates the second quarter (1 st July to 30 th September), 
 Q3 indicates the third quarter (1 st October to 31 st December) 
 and Q4 indicates the fourth quarter (1 st January to 31 st March) 
 Period: Select the period 
 for which user is paying tax. Set the period using calendar popup. Normally, 
 period equals to the Quarter of the financial year 
 Branch/Division : Enter the 
 branch name of the Company 
 Full Name: Enter full name 
 here 
 Designation: Enter designation 
 here 
 STD 
 Code: Enter the STD code of the company location 
 After 
 filling up the above fields, user will find an option as "Change 
 of address made since last TDS Return Submitted". Here, select "No", 
 if no change has been made since user's last TDS Return and select "Yes", 
 if there is any change of address made since last submission of TDS return. 
 Responsible Person Info 
 Select 
 the Responsible Person Info tab to find the following text-boxes: 
 Full Name: Enter full name 
 here 
 Designation: Enter designation 
 here 
 Address1 : 
 Enter address. User can continue putting address up to the Address5 field 
 State: Enter the name of 
 state here 
 Pin Code: Enter the Pin 
 Code here 
 E-mail: Enter e-mail address 
 here 
 STD code: Enter the STD 
 code of the state 
 Telephone No: Enter telephone 
 number 
 Remarks: Enter comments, 
 if any 
 After 
 entering data into all the necessary fields through ' General 
 Info ' and ' Responsible Person 
 Info ' tabs, now, user requires to click the ' Generate ' 
 button. 
 Once 
 the 'Generate' button is clicked, it will create an ASCII Text file, provided 
 no error occurs in the record. 
 In 
 the event any error occurs in the entry, those errors will be displayed 
 through a txt file. User can correct the file and re-upload. 
 Click 
 Save Selection button to 
 save all the entered details into the server database. 
 Click 
 Load Selection button to 
 show the previously saved data into respective fields. 
 Note: For E-TCS (Tax Collected at Source) 
 deposit, please check 27EQ drop 
 down button 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

 implication for Mobilization/Secure advance payment

 ‘Receipt/Payment’ and ‘Payment Requisition Option’. Initially, it was

 advance).

 no tax will be calculated but an implication of tax will be found during

 (like other Reverse charge advance payment) and subsequent TDS will also 
 be calculated.

 Requisition:

title: GSTIN Wise AUTO Hold/Release process based GSTR2A from Govt. GST Portal
text:
GSTIN Wise AUTO Hold/Release process based GSTR2A from Govt. GST Portal 
 Tutorial" />
 GSTIN Wise 
 AUTO Hold/Release process based GSTR2A from Govt. GST Portal 
 Auto 
 hold/release feature in Farvision retains 
 the unpaid tax amount of vendors based on their 
 filing status in the Government GST portal . 
 On 
 occasions, vendors' bills may be paid in full before they file GSTR-1, 
 leading to potential overpayment or loss of tax amounts, resulting in 
 operational inconsistencies. 
 To 
 manually monitor these discrepancies, one would need to individually track 
 the filing status of each vendor, a time-consuming process demanding considerable 
 effort to ensure accuracy. 
 To 
 address this issue, an automated process has been introduced. 
 Working Logic: 
 The Auto hold/release function operates on a scheduled 
 process that involves several steps. 
 1. Download of Data and Filing 
 Status : Firstly, the system automatically downloads the data and filing 
 status of vendors associated with each GSTIN from the Government GST portal 
 once a day. 
 2. Analysis of Unpaid Vendor Bills : 
 Secondly, the system analyses the unpaid bills of each vendor based on 
 their respective GSTINs. 
 3. Matching of Unpaid Bills : 
 Once all the necessary details are gathered, the system proceeds to identify 
 matching cases by comparing the Party Invoice Date, Party Invoice No, 
 Vendors' GSTIN, and BU GSTIN (Business Unit GSTIN) between the system's 
 unpaid bill-list and the downloaded data (GSTR-2A) from the Government 
 portal. 
 4. Checking of Filing status of 
 these Unpaid Bills (To Hold/Or To Release Tax Amount) : Once matching 
 cases are identified, the next step is to check the filing status of the 
 vendors. If the filing status is "Yes," then the corresponding 
 bills are eligible for release, and the system allows full payments without 
 any hold process. 
 However, if the filing status is not "Yes," 
 the system initiates an auto hold process and temporarily holds the tax 
 amount of the bills. 
 [Example: If an invoice of a vendor, ABC Enterprises 
 has a basic amount of Rs. 1000 with 18% GST (Rs. 180), the total payable 
 is Rs. 1180. If the vendor hasn't filed GSTR-1, the system holds the tax 
 amount (Rs. 180) automatically. The Hold-Release Report, under Accounts 
 Payable, marks this as 'HOLD- Auto Hold with tax Amount’. ] 
 5 . Release of Retained Tax Amount 
 after Invoice Filing Status Verification : On a scheduled basis, the 
 system repeats the same steps as before using new or updated downloaded 
 data. This includes checking for changes in filing statuses and any new 
 entries made in Farvision after the previous schedule process. The invoices, 
 which were on ‘Hold With Tax Amount’ previously, are ‘Released’ after 
 the successful filing status matched with GSTR-2A. 
 [So, in the above example, in the next scheduled 
 process, if the invoice filing status of ABC Enterprises, changes to 'Yes', 
 the system automatically releases the tax amount (Rs. 180), making the 
 invoice eligible for full payment. This is marked as 'Release- Auto Release' 
 in the Hold-Release Report under Accounts Payable.] 
 The process can be depicted in the 
 following diagram 
 The 
 Auto Hold/Release feature ensures that vendor bills are processed efficiently 
 and in compliance with filing statuses. By automating the analysis and 
 matching process, it reduces manual effort and improves accuracy in releasing 
 payments. 
 Pre-requisites 
 for enabling this process include the following: 
 1.The GSTIN of 
 the company must be registered on the Farvision GST Portal for the Auto 
 Hold/Release process to function, and if multiple GSTINs are to have these 
 features available, all GSTINs must be registered in the Farvision GST 
 portal on a per-GSTIN basis. 
 2. A cut-off date 
 must be decided to determine unpaid bills from vendors based on the invoice 
 date. 
 Here 
 are some important points to keep in mind: 
 1. 
 This process will only operate based on unpaid bills , and the outstanding 
 amount must be greater than the tax amount of the bill . 
 2. 
 Once the auto hold is implemented, it can only be released through the 
 scheduled process. Manual release is not permitted for auto hold cases. 
 3. 
 The system will not take into account any provisional unpaid bills. 
 Note: 
 This Facility/Service is available on subscription basis only.

title: Trial Balance
text:
Trial Balance 
 Queries" />
 Trial Balance 
 A trial 
 balance is 
 a list of all the general ledger accounts (both revenue and capital) contained 
 in the ledger of a business. The profit and loss statement and balance 
 sheet and 
 other financial reports can be produced using the ledger accounts listed 
 on the trial balance. 
 There are 
 filter options to filter the trial balance as Normal/Normal With Sub Account 
 Head/Group Wise/Group Wise With Account Head, Group Wise With Sub 
 Account Head 
 Filter 
 1 . 
 Select the Enterprise/Company/Business Unit for which report needs to 
 be generated 
 2. Select 
 the date range for the report to be generated 
 3. Click 
 on the Options 
 4. 
 Click on the Filter 
 5. The Filter 
 pop up will open 
 6. Select the Lakh, Crores or blank 
 in the first. The blank option will show data in their original values. 
 Options 
 1. Normal 
 2. Normal With Sub Account Head 
 3 . 
 Group Wise 
 4 . 
 Group Wise with Account Head 
 5 . 
 Group Wise with Sub Account Head 
 1. Normal 
 2. 
 Normal With Sub Account Head 
 3. 
 Group Wise 
 4. 
 Group Wise with Account Head 
 5. 
 Group Wise with Sub Account Head 
 User can 
 select any row and can drill down to the bottommost level of transaction. 
 Then if required the user can do necessary modifications of the transactions 
 also as shown below: 
 Trial 
 Balance - Normal

 in another tab called Level2

 called Level3 
 Level4: 
 On clicking any row in Level3 
 the month wise balance will be displayed in another tab called Level4 
 Level5: 
 On clicking any row in Level4 
 the specific month wise balance will be displayed in another tab called 
 Level5 
 On 
 clicking any document in Level5, the Account Heads, Parent Account Heads, 
 Cheque No.(If any), Cheque Date (If any), Narration (If any), Debit Amount 
 and Credit Amount will be displayed.

title: Cash Flow Classic
text:
Cash Flow Classic 
 Queries" />
 Cash Flow 
 Classic 
 Cash 
 flow is the movement of money in and out of a company. The cash flow statement 
 is a financial statement that reports on a company's sources and usage 
 of cash over a specified time period. A company's cash flow is typically 
 categorized as cash flows from operations, investing, and financing. In 
 Query Cash Flow Classic advantage over Cash Flow Classic report is that 
 user can drill and see the associated documents in the last level. 
 Enterprise/Company/Business Unit: 
 Select the Enterprise/Company/Business Unit for which report needs to 
 be populated. 
 Date Range: Select the Date Range 
 for which report needs to be generated. 
 Select 
 the Cash Flow Classic generation from the following options available 
 Normal(With 
 Provisional and without Provisional) 
 Normal 
 with Sub AccountHead(With Provisional and without Provisional) 
 Group 
 Wise with Sub AccountHead(With Provisional and without Provisional) 
 Group 
 Wise with AccountHead(With Provisional and without Provisional) 
 Filter Option 
 Click 
 on Cash flow Classic filter option 
 Select 
 the Options 
 Click 
 on Get Latest Data Check box 
 Select 
 the template 
 Select 
 the Financial Year 
 Click 
 on OK 
 Click 
 Refresh 
 Level 1 
 Level 2 
 Note : 
 Cash Flow Classic Report and Cash Flow Classic 
 Query will show the updated data after executing the Cash flow generation 
 process as mentioned above. In the 2nd level 
 all the details can be exported using the excel button. For the 1st level

 Configuration Process 
 Mobile Configuration 
 Mobile configuration is required for each mobile app (both IOS and android) to enable push notifications. For details about Enterprise Name, server public IP and app credentials, please refer to the detailed help on Mobile Configuration . 
 Download Farvision Approval App from 
 1. Apple Apps Store (For IOS) 
 2. Android Store (For Android) 
 Please type FV Approval on Google Play Store/Apple Apps Store to find and download the mobile application or download from the following URLs 
 Download Links 
 For IOS 
 https://apps.apple.com/in/app/farvisionapprovalr2/id1435066074 
 For Android 
 https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.gamut.farvisionapprovalr2&hl=en_IN&gl=US 
 Cloud SetUp 
 Step1: Install and open FV Approval App. Press 'Configure Your App' to setup your account. 
 Step2: Press ‘Cloud SetUp’ if your Farvision application runs on Farvision Cloud server. Please contact your administrator to know your cloud server name. Choose your cloud server from “Cloud SetUp” option. 
 Step3: After account configuration, enter ‘User Name’ and ‘Password’ and press ‘Login’. 
 OR 
 Set Up 
 Step1: Install and open FV Approval App. Press 'Configure Your App' to setup your account. Press ‘Set Up’. 
 Step2 : Enter your Enterprise name and on premises server URL/IP. HTTPS is required to be checked if your server is SSL certified and you have entered domain name. If you have entered IP Address as server url then SSL is not required hence left this unchecked. 
 Step3: After account configuration, enter ‘User Name’ and ‘Password’ and press ‘Login’.
